transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

My supervisor sent me here for an evaluation after pulling me off field duty because of how I've been performing on emergency calls. I feel like I’m moving wrong and doing the wrong things, like my actions don’t match what’s happening around me, and my crew says I’m acting really off. It's just getting really hard to keep up when everything is moving so fast around me.
When you feel like your actions don't match or you are moving wrong, does it feel like you are detached from your own body, almost like you are an outside observer watching yourself?

No, I don't really feel like an outside observer or completely detached from my body. It feels more like my body is just on a different channel, where I'll freeze up or move way too slowly to keep up with the emergency around me.
Have you experienced any highly stressful or traumatic events on the job, and do you find yourself having unwanted memories or flashbacks of those events?

Yes, about ten months ago I responded to a really chaotic multi-car collision on I-95 that left me feeling pretty shaken up. But I don't actually have any flashbacks, nightmares, or unwanted memories about the accident itself.
Have you recently experienced hearing voices that others can't hear, or felt like your thoughts or movements are being controlled by an outside force?

No, I haven't heard any voices that other people can't hear. I also don't feel like some outside force is controlling my thoughts or movements; it's just more like my own body isn't responding the way I want it to in the moment.
Have you been evaluated by a doctor or neurologist for these movement issues, and did they find any physical or neurological cause?

No, I haven't seen a neurologist or had any physical tests done for these movement issues. My supervisor just told me I had to get a psychiatric evaluation before I could be cleared to return to duty.
Do these episodes of freezing or moving slowly only happen during high-stress situations at work, or do they also occur during your normal, routine activities at home?

The freezing and slow movements mostly happen when I'm on scene during work calls, like when I find myself staring at my hands or slowly re-rolling bandages while everyone else is rushing. At home, I don't really have those freezing episodes; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired, mostly just sitting on the couch and doing nothing.
You mentioned feeling flat and tired at home. Over the past few weeks, have you also been feeling down, sad, or hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel actively sad, but I've completely lost interest in things I used to love like running, fishing, and playing basketball. I just feel incredibly flat and tired inside, so I spend my time sitting in my apartment, ignoring texts from my brother and friends because I can't find the energy to care or get off the couch.
How long have you been experiencing this extreme tiredness, lack of energy, and loss of interest in your usual activities?
It started about ten months ago, not long after that bad pileup on I-95. It's pretty much been going on like this for most of the past year now, and I just can't seem to get going.
Along with the lack of energy and loss of interest, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or how you feel about yourself over these past ten months?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite. As for how I feel about myself, I'm not really sure and haven't thought much about it, other than just feeling generally flat.

When you freeze up during emergency calls, does it feel like your muscles are physically paralyzed or too weak to move, or is it more like your mind goes blank and you are unsure of what action to take?

It’s not physical paralysis or weakness, but it feels like my body is on a completely different channel. I'll just stand there staring at my hands or start doing something weirdly slow and out of sync, like re-rolling bandages, while everyone else is moving fast around me. I know I'm off in those moments, but I just can't seem to snap into the right gear.
Over the past ten months, have you noticed any difficulties with your concentration, memory, or making simple everyday decisions?

Yes, I've really struggled with concentrating and processing information over the past ten months, especially at work. My partners have pointed out that I freeze during routine procedures and misinterpret simple directions from dispatch, because I just can't seem to get my brain and body into the right gear when things are moving fast.
During these past ten months, have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or that life is no longer worth living?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to die. Even though I feel really flat, tired, and disconnected from my life right now, I've never thought about ending things.
When you think about your future, do you find yourself feeling hopeless or having pessimistic thoughts about how things will turn out?
I don't really think about the future much right now, to be honest. I wouldn't say I feel actively hopeless or pessimistic, I just feel really flat, tired, and unmotivated most of the time.
Do you ever blame yourself for the accident ten months ago, or feel like you are failing or letting your crew down because of your current struggles?

No, I don't blame myself for the accident itself since I was just one of the EMTs responding to it. But I definitely feel like I'm letting my crew down and failing them now, especially since I've been pulled off duty and my confidence has taken such a big hit.
Have you ever had periods in your life, even for just a few days, where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, needing very little sleep, or like your mind was racing?

No, I've never had any times where I felt unusually energetic or didn't need to sleep. I've never experienced my mind racing like that either. Before all of this started, my energy levels were always pretty normal.
Have this flat feeling, lack of energy, and loss of interest been present nearly every day for most of the day over these past ten months, or do you have days where you feel like your normal self?

Yes, it's been pretty much every single day since that accident ten months ago. I don't really have days where I feel like my normal self anymore; it's just a constant, heavy flatness. Most days I just stay on the couch and ignore invites from my friends and my brother because I can't find the energy to care.
You mentioned your confidence has taken a big hit. Do you find yourself feeling worthless or like a failure as a person overall, or is that feeling mostly limited to your performance at work?

It's not really an abstract feeling of being a failure overall, but my confidence has tanked because my life has completely fallen apart. Being pulled from field duty, getting written up, and stopping seeing my friends or taking care of myself makes me feel extremely low. Seeing all these different areas of my life suffer is what's really hitting me hard.
Have you noticed any significant, unintentional change in your weight—either losing or gaining weight—over these past ten months?
I haven't really noticed or paid attention to any changes in my weight. I just haven't been keeping track of things like that lately.
Even if you haven't noticed major changes, have you been sleeping significantly more hours than usual, or are you having trouble falling or staying asleep?
Honestly, I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep. I'm not sure if I'm sleeping more or having trouble with it, I just feel tired all the time.
Before the accident ten months ago, have you ever experienced any periods in your life where you felt this same kind of flatness, extreme tiredness, or loss of interest for weeks at a time?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this flatness or loss of interest before that accident ten months ago. Before the pileup, I was really active, always going on early-morning runs, fishing with my brother, and playing basketball with my friends. This whole feeling of not caring and just sitting around is completely new to me.
You mentioned feeling 'flat' rather than sad. Would you describe this flatness as a constant feeling of emptiness or a low mood that is present for most of the day?

No, it's not really a low mood or feeling empty inside. It's more like I'm completely drained and lacking any motivation or care to do anything, like I just don't have the energy to get off the couch or answer a text. It feels more like a total absence of interest and energy rather than being sad.
Even if you haven't tracked your weight, have you noticed a decrease in your appetite, such as having to force yourself to eat or finding that food doesn't taste as good as before?
I haven't really noticed any change in my appetite or how food tastes. To be honest, it's just not something I've been paying attention to lately.
To help me understand the full picture, have you been using alcohol, recreational drugs, or any medications to help cope with these feelings over the past ten months?

No, I haven't been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or medications to cope with how I'm feeling. I don't really do any of that, I've just been sitting at home trying to get through the days on my own.
You mentioned that you've stopped taking care of yourself. Are you struggling with basic daily tasks like showering, dressing, or preparing meals, and how much effort does it take to do them?

Yes, taking care of myself has definitely taken a major hit since all of this started. I spend most of my time just sitting on the couch in my apartment, feeling completely flat and tired inside. I just lack the energy or motivation to care about anything, which makes even basic daily routines feel incredibly difficult to initiate.
During these times when you freeze up on calls, are you still able to speak and respond if someone talks to you, or do you find yourself completely silent and unable to talk?

I'm not really sure or haven't paid attention to whether I'm able to speak or if I stay completely silent during those moments. I just know that I feel completely frozen, out of sync, and unable to snap out of it. It's like my body is on a different channel and I just can't seem to get into the right gear.
Do you find that your low energy or flat feeling is consistently worse at a particular time of day, such as being much harder to handle in the morning?

I haven't really noticed any specific pattern or time of day when the flat and tired feeling is worse. It just feels pretty constant all the time, and I'm not sure if it changes from morning to night.
During those times when you freeze up, do you ever find yourself holding unusual or awkward physical positions for a long time, or do your muscles feel very stiff?

No, I don't really experience my muscles feeling stiff or holding awkward positions. When it happens, I just freeze up and find myself staring down at my hands while everyone else is moving fast around me.
When something positive happens, such as when your brother or friends try to reach out, do you feel any temporary lift in your mood, or do you remain completely flat and unable to react emotionally?

No, I don't feel any lift in my mood at all when they reach out. I just feel completely flat and indifferent inside, unable to care enough to reply or get off the couch. I remember really enjoying those activities in the past, but now I just can't feel anything.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any medical conditions, like thyroid problems or anemia, or have you had any recent blood work done to check for physical causes of your fatigue?
No, I'm not aware of any medical conditions like thyroid problems or anemia. I also haven't had any recent blood work done to check for things like that.
Have you noticed yourself waking up unusually early in the morning—say, two or more hours earlier than you used to—and finding it impossible to get back to sleep?
No, I haven't really noticed waking up that early or having that specific sleep issue. I'm just tired all the time, but I don't think I'm waking up hours before I need to.
